name: CapCut Apple-Style Slide-Up Text Stack
use_when: A social edit needs clean premium title text, caption-like emphasis, or presentation-style text movement.
Multiple short words should appear with the same smooth slide-up behavior but different positions.
The project tone supports restrained modern sans typography rather than loud meme text.
avoid_when: The message needs plain accessibility captions more than designed text.
The text is long enough that a 22-frame slide delays comprehension.
The frame has no negative space and the slide-up text would cover faces, proof, UI, or products.

timeline_pattern.pattern: add_text -> choose_modern_sans -> set_color_spacing_shadow -> first_transform_blend_keyframe -> 22_frame_later_keyframe -> start_opacity_0_y_offset_down -> cubic_ease_y_curve -> compound_template -> duplicate_compounds -> edit_words_and_positions
timeline_pattern.template_rule: Create one clean animated text compound, then duplicate and edit the internal words instead of rebuilding the animation for each word.
timeline_pattern.hierarchy_rule: Reposition and resize duplicated words so the eye has a clear reading order.
timeline_pattern.curve_rule: Use a cubic ease on Y movement so the text enters smoothly rather than linearly.

motion.rule: The slide should feel smooth and restrained, with the final text settled before reading becomes necessary.

keyframe_values.duration: About 22 frames between start and end keyframes is a useful CapCut starting point for premium slide-up text.
keyframe_values.start_y_offset: Move the starting text down, such as around -160 in CapCut's Y/value system from the tutorial context, then tune visually.
keyframe_values.easing: Use Cubic Ease on the Y curve and keep the bottom curve line mostly horizontal for a smooth professional settle.
keyframe_values.shadow: A very low-opacity shadow, around 7, can add separation without looking heavy.

sound.rule: Use no SFX or a very soft tick/whoosh only when the slide is a meaningful reveal; keep speech dominant.

captions.rule: Treat this as designed text. Suppress ordinary captions if they duplicate the same words, unless accessibility requires both.

color.rule: Use neutral off-white or off-gray text only where contrast remains strong over the footage.

implementation.ffmpeg: Animate drawtext y position and alpha over roughly 22 frames with an easing expression; use a subtle shadow and render a contact sheet for placement.
implementation.remotion: Create an AppleSlideText component with text, x/y, startFrame, durationFrames, opacity interpolation, translateY interpolation, cubic easing, and optional shadowOpacity.
implementation.blender: Animate text object location and material alpha with Bezier interpolation, then duplicate the animated object or parent to preserve timing.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Add a text layer, choose a clean bold sans font, tighten Character slightly if needed, set off-gray color, keyframe Transform and Blend, move about 22 frames, add landing keyframes, return to the first keyframe, set Opacity 0 and move the text downward, apply Cubic Ease to Y, add a low-opacity shadow, create a compound clip, duplicate it, and edit internal words/positions.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Essential Graphics text with Position and Opacity keyframes, Ease Out/Ease In or temporal Bezier, a subtle shadow, and nested/duplicated graphics for repeated words.

common_mistakes: Using the smooth slide on long phrases that should be read immediately.
Leaving duplicated compound words stacked on top of each other.
Using heavy shadow or pure white text where a neutral off-white would feel cleaner.
Forgetting to edit the internal text in duplicated compounds.
Letting ordinary captions duplicate the designed slide-up text.
qc: Does the text settle before the phrase needs to be read?
Do duplicated compound words have updated text, position, and hierarchy?
Does the cubic ease feel smooth rather than robotic or floaty?
Does the text avoid faces, proof, UI, products, and captions?
Does the subtle shadow improve separation without becoming visible styling?
